title: Smith v. Southwest Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained Smith’s appeal, reversed the lower courts’ judgments and the finding of guilt on all four charges, and annulled her suspension from the sacraments. It declined to remand for retrial because the evidence was insufficient.
first_summary: Smith appealed her conviction for divisiveness, gossip and slander, breaking membership vows, and contumacy. The SJC overturned the convictions and suspension because the documentary evidence did not prove the charges and the Session committed serious procedural errors, including trying the case without witnesses and placing the burden of proof on Smith. Although those errors could have required a new trial, no retrial was ordered because the evidence was insufficient.
summary: Smith appealed discipline for divisiveness, gossip and slander, broken membership vows, and contumacy arising largely from complaints and letters during church conflict. The SJC sustained her appeal, reversed guilt on all four charges, and annulled suspension from the sacraments. The documentary record proved none of the allegations; filing complaints was not itself divisiveness, and the trial improperly lacked a witness, shifted proof to Smith, showed prejudice, and unfairly rejected her written defense. The SJC declined remand because the evidence was insufficient.

evidence_notes.qualifications: Procedural errors could have warranted retrial, but the SJC declined remand because the evidence did not establish guilt; the suspension procedure was also seriously defective; lines 205–213, 276–307 (printed pp. 225–228).
